text:
Running an algo in India in 2026 is very different from running one in 2024.

SEBI's retail algo framework has been fully mandatory for brokers since 1 April 2026. Here's what it changed for traders in practice:

• Every automated order now carries an exchange-assigned Algo ID, so each order can be traced to its strategy.
• API access is tied to a whitelisted static IP. Orders from any other IP get rejected.
• Daily authentication and 2FA are part of the routine now.
• Algos must run through the broker's controlled environment, with a kill switch.
• Strategies that cross the order-rate threshold, and black-box strategy providers, have extra registration requirements.

My take: this is good for serious traders. It filters out people who sell "guaranteed" algos, and it rewards anyone who builds a clean, documented and compliant setup.

If you're an algo trader still working out static IPs, broker APIs or registration, let's connect. Getting the infrastructure right is half the work.

Is your setup fully compliant yet? Tell me in the comments.
